To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the angular spectrum of laser radiation in a plasma depends on the electron density profile in the active medium, which in turn depends on the laser pulse intensity.
we investigated the angular spectrum of plasma laser emission influenced by features of optical properties of the plasma.

the divergence of laser radiation in a laser-plasma depends on the electron density profile in the active medium and that the angular spectrum of the stimulated emission can be used to determine the electron density profile.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the angular spectrum of plasma laser light.
the angular spectrum of laser radiation from a plasma, which is influenced by the optical properties of a plasma medium.
the influence of the optical properties (the gain and refractive index) of the active medium on the angular spectrum of radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study has demonstrated that, for the first time, a laser plasma has been used as a gain medium in a laser system.

the angular spectrum of laser radiation is a sensitive indicator of the optical properties and structure of the active medium, and that the divergence of laser radiation is determined not only by the gain profile and the phase of the radiation, but also by its angular spectrum.
the authors have not demonstrated any evidence that the angular distribution of radiation from laser plasma is determined by the electron density profile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the angular distribution of the radiation in a laser discharge can be calculated by using the angular spectrum of radiation and the angular spectrum of the optical properties.
we have demonstrated the importance of accounting for the optical properties of a laser plasma when analyzing the angular distribution of the laser radiation.

the angular divergence of laser radiation is determined by the spatial distribution of the gain coefficient in the active medium, and the divergence is not determined by the electron density distribution in the plasma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a homogeneous gain distribution can be assumed for a plasma with a density profile that is not too steep.
the angular spectrum of radiation in the plasma laser is influenced by the features of the optical characteristics of the active medium and the angular spectrum of spontaneous radiation.
the divergence of laser radiation can be used as a diagnostic of the plasma optical properties.
